TulsaConnect's Downtown Tulsa facility (DC-5) sits on the city's downtown underground power grid with fully redundant A and B power infrastructure, multiple cooling sources, and numerous on-site fiber carriers. The operator does not publish a specific power capacity or square footage for this building, making it impossible to estimate its scale relative to other AI infrastructure. This downtown location is one of three geographically diverse facilities TulsaConnect operates statewide, with an aggregate company capacity exceeding 400 racks across all sites combined.

Oklahoma has nine mapped data center facilities but no published megawatt figures from any operator, leaving DC-5 unranked by capacity within the state. The facility is one of two near-identical mapped entities roughly 550 meters apart in downtown Tulsa, both applied to the same address because TulsaConnect's own website names only one downtown facility and the registry could not determine which mapped point more precisely represents the actual building.

TulsaConnect has operated in Oklahoma since 1996 and describes itself as the state's oldest locally owned data center provider. Without published power or space specifications for DC-5, or confirmation of which mapped entity represents the building, this facility cannot be assessed as a constraint or enabler of AI scaling in the region. The downtown location's access to redundant power and fiber suggests infrastructure suitable for enterprise or managed services workloads rather than the density requirements of current AI training campuses.
